item.title: Current Events - September 16, 2026
item.description:
September 16, 2026 (2026-09-16) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Gaza war, Gaza genocide
      • Twenty-one people are killed, 45 are injured, and about 100 others are missing after a residential building in Gaza City collapses after it was previously hit by an Israeli airstrike. Twelve children are among the fatalities. (AFP via France 24) (Al Jazeera)

Arts and culture

  • 2026 Americana Music Honors & Awards
    • The Americana Music Honors & Awards are held at the Ryman Auditorium in Nashville, Tennessee, United States, with the Heartbreakers performing for the first time since lead vocalist Tom Petty's death in 2017. (The Independent)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026–2027 El Niño event
    • Guatemala announces food aid for about 1.2 million families affected by severe El Niño-related drought, which damages crops and livestock across the Dry Corridor. The programme distributes maize, beans, and rice with World Food Programme support. (AFP via Arab News)
  • At least 82 people are killed when a gold mine explodes in West Kordofan, Sudan, an area under control of the Rapid Support Forces. (Al Jazeera) (Sky News)

Health and environment

  • 2026 United Kingdom heatwaves
    • The United Kingdom records its second-best butterfly season in 16 years amidst record heat waves in the country. (The Independent)
  • Fiji declares HIV a national crisis after reporting 2,016 new diagnoses in 2025, sixteen times the 2019 total. The government estimates that one in 60 adults lives with HIV and expands testing, prevention, and treatment services. (AFP via New Straits Times)
  • In a study published by the Nature Medicine journal, scientists report that the PANXEON blood test helps detect pancreatic cancer at early stages and treat the disease before it spreads. (Scientific American) (Discover)

International relations

  • Canada–European Union relations
    • European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen invites Canada to become the first associate member of the European Union amidst the ongoing trade war between Canada and the United States. (CNBC)
  • International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war
    • The United States House of Representatives passes a bipartisan sanctions bill that imposes sanctions on Russia's energy revenues, financial institutions, officials, and shadow fleet, while authorizing tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian oil and gas. The bill will head to president Donald Trump's desk for his signature for it to become law. (Kyiv Independent) (Reuters)
  • The first summit between South Korea and the five countries of Central Asia is held in Seoul. (Euronews) (AFP via Korea Times) (Al Jazeera)

Law and crime

  • North Korea–South Korea relations
    • Inter-Korean Liaison Office bombing
      • A district court in Seoul, South Korea, orders North Korea to pay KRW 44.6 billion (US$32.5 million) in damages for destroying the Inter-Korean Liaison Office in Kaesong in 2020, in South Korea's first damages lawsuit against North Korea. (AFP via CNA) (Reuters)
  • Human rights in Macau
    • Macau begins its first closed-door national security trial against former legislator Au Kam San, who faces charges including subversion of state power and alleged ties with foreign groups and media outlets. He faces up to 25 years in prison. (AFP via RTL Today)
  • War crimes in the Kosovo War
    • The Kosovo Specialist Chambers sentences former prime minister Hashim Thaçi to 25 years in prison after convicting him on charges of murder, torture, cruel treatment and arbitrary detention committed during the Kosovo War. (AP)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Bangsamoro Parliament election
    • The Philippine Commission on Elections proclaims all 78 elected members of the Bangsamoro Parliament, with four parties given all seats for party representation. The Bangsamoro Federalist Party, earning most of the seats, fails to secure a majority, leading to a hung parliament. Meanwhile, six sectoral seats are given to the United Bangsamoro Justice Party. (Al Jazeera) (Manila Bulletin)

Science and technology

  • NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter discovers a recently formed crater on the moon larger than the Colosseum in Rome, Italy. (Phys.org)

Sports

  • In association football, Clearlake Capital buys out Todd Boehly and Mark Walter's stakes to gain full control of Premier League club Chelsea. The deal is valued at around £950 million (€1.1 billion) for the 25% share. Chelsea is now worth about £5 billion (€5.8 billion). (BBC Sport) (The Guardian) (ESPN)
  • The Women's Tennis Association (WTA) announces that its finals will move from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, to the Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina, United States, for three years beginning in 2027. The WTA also relocates its global headquarters from St. Petersburg, Florida, to Charlotte. (BBC)

item.title: Current Events - September 09, 2026
item.description:
September 9, 2026 (2026-09-09) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • 2026 Yemen offensive, Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict
        • September 2026 Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
          • Saudi Arabia launches 32 airstrikes in four governorates in Yemen against the Houthis. (UA News)
        • The death toll from the Saudi airstrike against a prison in Al-Jawf Governorate, two days ago, increases to 23 people. (AP)
    • Gaza war
      • Aftermath of the Second Intifada
        • Hamas claims that the Israel Defense Forces has killed Farah Hamed, a senior member who was accused of carrying out the 2003 attack that resulted in the killing of Shalom Har-Melech [he], the late husband of Limor Son Har-Melech, in a airstrike in the Gaza Strip. (The Jerusalem Post) (Israel National News) (VINnews)
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
        • Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launch missiles at the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Azraq, Jordan, reporting damage to maintenance facilities, deployment areas, and hangars. Jordan says its forces have intercepted 18 Iranian missiles, following United States strikes that destroyed five Iranian oil tankers. (AFP via France 24)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • A Russian drone strike hits a shopping centre in Sumy, Ukraine, killing two people and injuring 20 others. (Reuters)

Arts and culture

  • Death and state funeral of Harald V
    • The state funeral of King Harald V takes place at the Oslo Cathedral in Oslo, Norway. (CNN) (The New York Times)
  • The Tooro Kingdom in western Uganda selects Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, a television news anchor and editor, as its new monarch following the death of Rukidi IV last month. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • MV June Aster ship fire
    • Five people are killed and 87 others are reported missing when a fire breaks out aboard a passenger ferry off Coron, Palawan, Philippines. The coast guard rescues 42 people from the vessel, which carried 117 passengers and 17 crew members. (AFP via The Straits Times)
  • Sokolniki Suche train collision
    • A train collides with a truck at a level crossing in Sokolniki Suche, Poland, killing one person and injuring 20 others. (TVP World) (Xinhua)
  • Fourteen people are killed and eleven others are injured in an explosion at a weapons depot in Sarmada, Syria. (AP)
  • Two people are killed and extensive damage is caused after an explosion at a hydroelectric power station in Piotta, Ticino, Switzerland. (Reuters)

Health and environment

  • 2026 heat waves
    • 2026 European heatwaves
      • Peninsular Spain records its hottest summer since the State Meteorological Agency's measurements began in 1961, with an average temperature of 24.5 °C (76.1 °F) and 61 heatwave days from June through August. (Arab News Pakistan)
    • 2026 North American heat wave
      • The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration reports that the United States has experienced its hottest summer on record from June to August with a 23.6 °C (74.5 °F), surpassing the Dust Bowl. (Al Jazeera) (CBS News)
    • The Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) reports that August 2026 is the hottest month globally since measurements began, with an average temperature of 16.96 °C (62.53 °F), exceeding the previous record set in July 2023. (AP)
  • 2026 Indonesia wildfires
    • The C3S reports that wildfires in Kalimantan and Sumatra, Indonesia, produced more than 19.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions from September 1 to 7, the world's highest total and more than one-third of global fire emissions. (Reuters)

International relations

  • Israel–Slovenia relations
    • Israel opens its first embassy in Ljubljana, Slovenia. (AP)
  • Syria and weapons of mass destruction
    • The International Atomic Energy Agency ends its investigation into Syria's nuclear activities after the new government granted inspectors access to nuclear sites. Its board terminates a 2011 resolution that found Syria in non-compliance with its nuclear safeguards obligations. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • Reform UK financial allegations
    • The Metropolitan Police launch a criminal investigation into Reform UK over allegations that it broke foreign funding laws in the United Kingdom, following an investigation by Channel 4 News. (AP) (BBC News)
  • Brazilian Supreme Court president Edson Fachin suspends conflicting rulings by two justices, allowing Federal Police chief Andrei Rodrigues to remain in office while the court reviews allegations that police monitored justice André Mendonça and other government authorities. (Reuters)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Serbian parliamentary election
    • Serbian president Aleksandar Vučić dissolves the National Assembly and calls a snap parliamentary election for October 25, following a government proposal amid prolonged political tensions. The ruling Serbian Progressive Party nominates Vučić as its lead candidate and candidate for prime minister. (Xinhua)
  • Protests against the 2026 Iran war
    • Anti-war demonstrators in South Korea near the U.S. Embassy in Seoul gather to oppose and urge the government not to deploy troops to the Strait of Hormuz. (ABS-CBN) (Middle East Eye)

Science and technology

  • 2026 in archosaur paleontology
    • Scientists at the Denver Museum of Nature and Science in Colorado, U.S., and Liverpool John Moores University in England discover the first adult Tyrannosaurus trackway at Hell Creek Formation in North Dakota, U.S. The study is published in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology. (Phys.org) (Axios)

item.title: Current Events - September 15, 2026
item.description:
September 15, 2026 (2026-09-15) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • Oman's maritime security centre reports that two sailors are reported to be missing after the Panama-flagged oil tanker El Gaia was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz near the Musandam Peninsula. (BBC News)
      • Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war
        • The Kuwaiti energy ministry reports that Kuwait's electrical grid has held despite attacks from Iran against it. (Arab Times Kuwait)
    • Yemeni civil war
      • 2026 Yemen offensives
        • The United Nations reports that more than 100,000 people have fled their homes in western and southern Yemen due the ongoing Houthi offensive against Yemeni government forces, and that 2,400 refugees have arrived in Djibouti in the last four days alone. (Kurdistan 24)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • A drone crosses from Belarusian airspace into Lithuania before being shot down by a NATO fighter jet over the village of Pratkūnai, Kaišiadorys District Municipality, near Kruonis Pumped Storage Plant, two days after an unidentified object flew over Lithuanian airspace from Belarus to Kaliningrad Oblast, Russia. (BBC News) (LRT)

Business and economy

  • 2026–2027 El Niño event
    • The Panama Canal Authority reduces daily ship transits through the canal from 36 to 32 as below-average rainfall and a strengthening El Niño lower water levels in reservoirs supplying the waterway. (DW)
  • Kenya announces bans on exports of unprocessed gold and establishes at least three refineries, seeking to maximize its economic value by increasing domestic processing. (Nairametrics)

Disasters and accidents

  • Six people die while 17 others are injured after an Elf truck, with an Isabela–Benguet route and carrying 27 passengers, plunges into a ravine in Bontoc, Mountain Province, Philippines. (Philippine Daily Inquirer)
  • Three people die when a telecopter operated by KNBC in Los Angeles, California, United States, crashes while covering a fatal collision of an SUV and a Los Angeles Metro bus, in Chatsworth. (AP) (BBC News)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • The United Nations reports that daily Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo declined from about 120 to 80, while 10 of 62 affected health zones record no new infections for more than 22 days. (The Independent)
  • Aging of Japan
    • Japan's health ministry reports 107,677 people aged 100 or older, exceeding 100,000 for the first time since records began in 1963. (AFP via The Manila Times) (CNN)

International relations

  • Denmark–Russia relations
    • A Russian Navy warship fires two flares at a Danish military helicopter in the Baltic Sea. (The Guardian)

Law and crime

  • 2024 Bangladesh quota reform movement, Controversies related to Sheikh Hasina, Capital punishment in Bangladesh
    • A court in Bangladesh sentences seven Awami League leaders who were former officials in former prime minister Sheikh Hasina's government to death in absentia over their role in deadly crackdowns on the anti-government protests in 2024. (DW)
  • Death of Noah Donohoe
    • The Northern Irish jury in the inquest returns a narrative verdict, criticising the Department for Infrastructure for failure to prevent public access to the tunnel Donohoe was found in and the police for failures in their investigation. (RTÉ)
  • Femicide in Latin America, Gender inequality in El Salvador
    • A court in El Salvador sentences a man to life imprisonment for aggravated femicide and stalking, the first such sentence for femicide in the country's history. (DW)
  • Phillips family disappearances
    • A New Zealand inquiry finds that police and Oranga Tamariki failed to act on warnings that Tom Phillips might abduct his three children and possessed firearms, contributing to missed opportunities to prevent or end their nearly four-year disappearance. (AFP via France 24)
  • The Brazilian public prosecutor's office files a civil action against Vale, the world's largest iron ore producer and one of Brazil's biggest companies, as well as the national mining agency and the Minas Gerais state government. The lawsuit is based on a containment overflow of two sumps at the Mina de Viga site in Congonhas in January, which caused the site to be shut down. (Mining Reports) (The Rio Times)
  • China implements new travel regulations allowing exit bans on citizens who violate technology import or export controls or commit national-security-related offences abroad. Returned citizens can face bans lasting six months to three years. (AFP via Dawn)
  • Former Golden Dawn spokesperson Ilias Kasidiaris is released from prison in Domokos, Phthiotis, Greece, after serving part of a 13-year sentence for leading a criminal organization and announces plans to return to politics, although he remains barred from office until 2033. (AFP) (The National Herald)
  • ProRail services across northern and central parts of the Netherlands are disrupted by a sabotage operation after pipes are attached to tracks, resulting in the failure of railway signals. (Reuters) (BBC News) (Politico Europe)
  • Romanian farmers clash with gendarmes in Bucharest during protests against live export restrictions due to ovine rinderpest and other policies. The confrontations leave 24 people injured, including eight gendarmes, while police detain 26 protesters. (AFP via France 24) (Bloomberg)

Politics and elections

  • Reactions to the 2026 Iran war
    • United States representative Thomas Massie files articles for impeachment against defense secretary Pete Hegseth for allegedly violating the War Powers Resolution by declaring war against Iran without congressional approval. (Hindustan Times) (Military.com)

Sports

  • 2026 Asian Games
    • The Italian cruise ship Costa Serena docks in Nagoya, Japan, to house about 4,000 Asian Games athletes and officials as delegations report accommodation problems, including undersized beds, leaking sinks, and room shortages. (AFP via France 24)
  • In association football, UEFA announces that the Champions League finals in 2028 and 2029 will be held at the Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany, and Camp Nou in Barcelona, Spain, respectively. (Al Jazeera)
  • The World Athletics Championships in 2029 and 2031 are awarded to Nairobi, Kenya, and Munich, Germany, respectively. 2029 will mark the first time the event is held on the continent of Africa. (The Star Kenya) (AP)

item.title: Current Events - September 08, 2026
item.description:
September 8, 2026 (2026-09-08) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Yemeni civil war
    • 2026 Yemen offensive, Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict
      • September 2026 Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
        • Houthi forces launch ballistic missiles and drones at several locations in Saudi Arabia, injuring 73 people, including civilians, and causing fires that temporarily halt operations at some energy facilities. (Reuters)
      • The confirmed toll of the offensive in western Yemen increases to 500 people killed, including 278 Houthi fighters, 216 soldiers of the Yemeni Armed Forces and 29 civilians. (AFP via LBC Group)
      • The toll from yesterday's Saudi airstrike against a prison in Al-Jawf Governorate increases to 17 people killed and seven more wounded. (Saba News Agency)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Kyiv strikes, Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Russia launches drones and missiles at Kyiv, Ukraine, following a weekend pause in strikes, killing five people and injuring at least 10. The attacks damage civilian infrastructure at at least 16 locations and cause fires in five districts. (The Pioneer) (Reuters)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Kordofan campaign
      • Around 13 people are killed in a drone strike by the Rapid Support Forces on a courthouse in Umm Ruwaba, North Kordofan. (Sudan Horizon)
    • Peace talks are held by mediators from the African Union, the Intergovernmental Authority on Development, the Arab League, the European Union and the United Nations, in Khartoum, Sudan, in an effort to end the three-year long civil war, with UN envoy Pekka Haavisto attending the talks. (Arab News)

Business and economy

  • Canada–United States relations
    • 2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
      • Canada's retaliatory tariffs of 15% to 50% on CA$27.6 billion (US$19.9 billion) of U.S. goods, including steel, dairy products, appliances, agricultural equipment, paper products, and electronics, take effect in response to U.S. tariffs on Canadian imports. (AFP via France 24)
      • In response, the United States announces a ban on the imports of Canadian alcoholic drinks, motorcycles, and dairy products beginning September 29. (Reuters)
  • International sanctions against Iran
    • United States sanctions against Iran, Economic D-Day
      • The U.S. treasury department imposes sanctions against 27 Iranian airlines, including flag carrier Iran Air, in an effort to squeeze Iran's economy. (Al-Monitor)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Nepal–Tibet floods
    • The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority reports that 13,583 people have been rescued so far since flash floods ravaged Nepal. (The Rising Nepal)
  • A MBB Bo 105 helicopter operating for the Flying Doctors of Malaysia crashes near Long Lellang, Sarawak, Malaysia, killing all five onboard. (Reuters) (The Star)
  • Indonesia reopens its airport in Jakarta and four others after previously being closed due to ashes from Anak Krakatoa. (Al Jazeera)

Health and environment

  • 2026 North American heat wave
    • A third-year student in the marching band at the University of Iowa in Iowa City, U.S., dies after collapsing during extreme heat at the Iowa Hawkeyes season opener at Kinnick Stadium. Temperatures reached 94 °F (34 °C) at the time of the game. (The Guardian) (The Athletic via The New York Times)
  • Famine in Sudan
    • A famine is reported across Sudan's Jebel Marra area in the Darfur region, with 20 people dying from hunger and diseases. (Sudan Tribune)
  • Health effects arising from the September 11 attacks
    • Mayor Zohran Mamdani says that New York City, U.S., has released over 170,000 documents detailing that city officials knew about the air quality and unsafe conditions at the time of the September 11 attacks including at Ground Zero. (CNN) (The Guardian)
  • Indonesia's food agency suspends nearly 2,000 kitchens in its national free meals programme after they fail to register for mandatory sanitation inspections, as the agency strengthens food safety measures following widespread food poisoning cases. (Reuters)

International relations

  • Morocco–Spain relations
    • 2026 Ceuta migrant crisis
      • Spain declassifies around 40 intelligence reports concerning the July migrant crisis into Ceuta, during which more than 70,000 people crossed from Morocco, amid scrutiny of whether Moroccan security forces facilitated the crossings and whether Spanish security services had prior warning of the influx. (AFP via RFI)
  • Israel–United Kingdom relations, Israeli occupation of the West Bank, Legality of Israeli settlements
    • The United Kingdom announces it will ban imports of all goods from Israeli settlements in the West Bank, as well as some services, including financing, construction, infrastructure, real estate, and advertising. (Telegraph India)
    • To reciprocate the UK sanctions, Israel announces it will close the UK consulate in East Jerusalem. Israel also forbids the UK from participating in the U.S.-led mission for Gaza, and bans some British officials, including former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, from entering the country. (The North West Star)
  • Bosnia and Herzegovina–Serbia relations
    • Bosnia and Herzegovina declares two Serbian embassy diplomats, military attaché Milan Dulanović and Security Intelligence Agency representative advisor at the embassy Darko Maksimović, as personae non gratae after attending the funeral of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić in Belgrade. (Reuters)
  • Nicaragua v. Germany, German support for Israel in the Gaza war
    • Nicaragua urges the International Court of Justice to reject Germany's objections to its case, stating that German arms exports to Israel breach the Genocide Convention and international humanitarian law. Germany responds by saying that the court lacks jurisdiction over parts of the case. (AFP via France 24) (Al Jazeera)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Musée Renoir theft
    • Thieves steal Jeune Femme au puits and Madame Colonna Romano [fr] by Pierre-Auguste Renoir from the Musée Renoir in Cagnes-sur-Mer, Alpes-Maritimes, France. The works have an estimated value of €9 million. (BBC News)

Science and technology

  • AI boom
    • OpenAI says that it has solved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem, with the announcement raising questions about plagiarism. (BBC News) (Scientific American)

item.title: Current Events - September 17, 2026
item.description:
September 17, 2026 (2026-09-17) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Gaza war
      • Israeli government response to the October 7 attacks
        • Lt. Col. "Aleph", the chief police officer in the Southern Command's Gaza Division, is dismissed following his role in the failures leading to the Hamas-led October 7 attacks on Israel. (The Times of Israel)
      • The Israel Defense Forces confirm that they have killed a Al-Qassam Brigades Nukhba Forces commander who took part in the October 7 attacks in a airstrike and a Hamas navy officer in another airstrike in Gaza City. (Israel National News) (JFeed)
    • 2026 Iran war
      • US war crimes in Iran strikes
        • The UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission finds "reasonable grounds" that the United States military may have committed war crimes with attacks on the Minab school and Lamerd sports hall in southern Iran. (Reuters)
    • Yemeni civil war
      • 2026 Yemen offensives
        • Al-Akhbar reports that Saudi Arabia has sent a proposal for Oman to mediate a two-week ceasefire with the Houthis. (AzerNews)
        • A Yemeni resident is reported to be killed by debris from a drone in Taif, Mecca Province. (Arab News)
  • Aftermath of the South Sudanese Civil War
    • Twenty-six people are killed and 82 more injured during clashes between two rival communities in Abyei, at the border between Sudan and South Sudan. (Al Jazeera)
  • Fifteen civilians are killed during an armed attack by unknown individuals in Madegoua, Far North Region, Cameroon. (Reuters)

Arts and culture

  • France–Mexico relations
    • The 16th-century Codex Azcatitlan goes on display in Mexico City after France loaned two folios nearly two centuries after the manuscript left the country. Mexico continues seeking the codex's permanent return from France. (AFP) (BBC News)

Health and environment

  • Environmental policy of the second Trump administration
    • The United States Fish and Wildlife Service narrows its enforcement of the Endangered Species Act by excluding unintentional wildlife deaths from its definition of prohibited take, including foreseeable deaths linked to activities such as commercial fishing and logging. (AFP via France 24)
  • Biologists publish a study in the journal Current Biology describing a new species of wild cat belonging to the genus Leopardus, commonly called the "tilcayo", in the Yungas cloud forests of Bolivia. This discovery marks the first new cat species in over 100 years. (Cell) (Reuters)
  • The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence approves the Trastuzumab deruxtecan drug for women in England with metastatic or incurable HER2-breast cancer that cannot be removed surgically, making it the first licensed targeted treatment for patients, two years after it was rejected due to its cost effectiveness. (Sky News) (The Independent)

International relations

  • Eighty-First session of the United Nations General Assembly, Palestine and the United Nations
    • The United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) votes 152–3, with four abstentions, to allow Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas and other senior Palestinian officials to address UN meetings, including the general debate of the eighty-first session of the UNGA, by video for one year after United States visa restrictions prevented their travel to New York City, where the UN headquarters are. (Reuters)
  • Israel–Serbia relations
    • Serbian president Aleksandar Vučić inaugurates a factory for Israeli-made drones that will be produced by the country's Krušik company, with Vučić stating that it will employ 100 people and produce advanced equipment for the Serbian military. (AP)

Law and crime

  • Human rights in Pakistan
    • Pakistan's Supreme Court suspends 17-year prison sentences imposed on human rights lawyer Imaan Mazari and her husband over anti-state social media posts, and grants them bail pending an Islamabad High Court ruling. (Reuters)
  • Malawian police rescue a 47-year-old British woman after her abduction in Blantyre. Four suspected kidnappers are killed in a shootout with officers, while a senior police officer is injured and hospitalized in stable condition. (AP via ABC News)
  • Thirty-seven suspected illegal gold miners die in custody of Nigeria's civil defence agency in Minna, Niger State. Survivors say overcrowding and poor ventilation caused breathing difficulties, while an intelligence report links the deaths to those conditions. The government orders an investigation. (AFP)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Swedish general election
    • Ulf Kristersson announces his resignation as Prime Minister of Sweden after his right-wing bloc wins 173 seats in the Riksdag, compared to 176 won by the opposition, led by Magdalena Andersson. (Al Jazeera) (BBC News)
  • Censorship and media control during the Venezuelan presidential crisis
    • Venezuela restores access to 17 news websites that were previously blocked, including EFE, El Nacional, NTN24, and Semana, as the interim government and opposition resume political transition talks that include freedom of expression. (AFP via Gulf News)
  • Visa policy of Australia
    • Australia tightens visa rules for international students and working holidaymakers, restricts visa switching, and increases enforcement against overstayers as it seeks to reduce net overseas migration to 225,000 by 2027–28 and ease pressure on housing. (AFP via France 24)

item.title: Current Events - September 10, 2026
item.description:
September 10, 2026 (2026-09-10) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • 2026 Yemen offensives
        • Houthis capture the port city of Mokha, as government forces retreat from the districts of Hays and Al Khawkhah. A mass exodus of civilians from the area towards Aden is reported. (AFP via France 24)
    • Gaza war
      • Aftermath of the Second Intifada
        • The Israel Defense Forces and Shin Bet confirm that they have killed Hamas senior leader Farah Hamed, a senior member who was accused of carrying out the 2003 attack that resulted in the killing of Shalom Har-Melech [he], the late husband of Limor Son Har-Melech, in a airstrike in the Gaza Strip. (Israel National News) (The Times of Israel)
      • Israeli airstrikes on the Gaza Strip kill a family of four. (Reuters)
    • Hezbollah–Israel conflict
      • 2026 Lebanon war
        • Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz claims that the Israeli military has destroyed a Hezbollah tunnel in Ali al-Taher. (The Financial Times) (Al Jazeera)
        • The U.S. Geological Survey reports that a magnitude 4.1 earthquake has been detected after Israel carried out the strike in Ali al-Taher. (Sky News)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war, Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Russia drone strikes across Ukraine kill at least 15 people and injure 90 others, including victims in Dnipro, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Pavlohrad, and Sumy. Ukraine also strikes gas facilities in Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug, Ural, Russia. (Al Jazeera)
    • Foreign fighters in the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Amnesty International says that Russia recruited foreign nationals for its war in Ukraine through deception, coercion, and exploitation, including false job offers and threats. The organization concludes that many such cases amount to human trafficking under international law. (The Eastleigh Voice)
  • Multiple projectile explosives believed to originate from Iraq strike pumping stations along the East–West Crude Oil Pipeline in Saudi Arabia, causing a fire. (CNN)

Business and economy

  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
      • Crude oil prices in the United States, including from Brent Crude and West Texas Intermediate, reach US$100, the highest since May, amidst the country's renewed tensions with Iran. (CNBC)
      • The European Central Bank raises its three key interest rates by 0.25 percentage points, lifting the deposit rate to 2.50%, as higher energy prices linked to the Iran war increase inflation pressures across the eurozone. (CNBC)
    • The International Monetary Fund reports that the global growth of the global economy is on track to reach 3% in 2026 despite the war in Iran, but also cautioned that risks still remain high. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • At least 20 people are killed and five others are reported missing after a fire breaks out on a cargo ship in Qingdao, Shandong, China. (CNN)
  • Five people are killed and 40 others are injured after a bus carrying Dutch tourists crashes between Zernez and Susch, Switzerland. (AP)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
    • Seven more children die from suspected measles in Bangladesh in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of deaths in the country to 1,009. (The Business Standard)
    • Health minister Sardar Md. Sakhawat Husain announces that Bangladesh will resume nationwide vaccinations beginning on September 25 amidst the ongoing measles outbreak. (South Asian Herald)

International relations

  • Algeria–United Arab Emirates relations
    • Algeria cuts diplomatic relations with the United Arab Emirates, without specifying a reason. (Reuters)
  • Peru–United States relations, War on drugs
    • Peruvian president Keiko Fujimori announces that Peru will join the U.S.-led Shield of the Americas coalition against drug cartels following a visit from U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Hutch Organised Crime Gang
    • An Irish court charges Jason Hutch, a son of alleged crime boss Gerry Hutch, with facilitating a criminal organisation, the same day he was extradited from Spain. (RTÉ)
  • Sri Lanka's Supreme Court overturns a 2019 presidential pardon granted to Buddhist monk Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara and orders him to serve the remainder of his six-year prison sentence for criminally intimidating human rights activist Sandya Eknelygoda. (AFP via France 24)

Science and technology

  • The first robotic surgical system in Kyrgyzstan is introduced at the Kyrgyz State Medical Academy. (Azertag) (AKIPress) (Caspian Post)

item.title: Current Events - September 20, 2026
item.description:
September 20, 2026 (2026-09-20) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Iran war ceasefire
      • Qatar as a mediator in conflict
        • Qatar's foreign ministry says that they are working to resume ceasefire negotiations between Iran and the United States. (Middle East Eye)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Ukrainian forces launch a massive drone attack on Moscow Oblast, Russia, with more than 1,600 long-range drones launched from Ukraine. At least two people are killed with hundreds more evacuated while Moscow Refinery is on fire following several direct hits. (Al Jazeera)
      • Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirms he ordered the attack on Moscow in response to Russian forces targeting civilians in Ukrainian cities, saying that FP-5 Flamingo cruise missiles and ballistic missiles were also used in the attack. (L'Unione Sarda)

Business and economy

  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • The Statistical Center of Iran reports that the country's gross domestic product contracted 10.1% year-on-year from late March to late June, during the war, amid longstanding sanctions and currency depreciation. (AFP via The Straits Times)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
    • The National Hurricane Center reports that Tropical Depression Six strengthened into Tropical Storm Fay amidst an unusually quiet Atlantic hurricane season caused by El Niño, becoming the sixth named storm of the season. (AccuWeather) (WFLA-TV)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • The Democratic Republic of the Congo launches vaccinations for frontline workers amdist the Ebola outbreak in the country. (Africanews)

International relations

  • France–Iran relations
    • Iranian authorities close down a French language centre affiliated with the French embassy in Tehran under a judicial order. Prosecutors say it operated without a licence and conducted activities against Iranian culture and national security. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Assassination of Jovenel Moïse, Haiti–United States relations
    • Haiti sends 18 suspects in the July 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moïse to the United States to face federal charges related to the killing. (Reuters)
  • Pakistani police arrest businesswoman Aleema Khan, sister of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan, at her home in Lahore, Punjab, one week before his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party's planned protest march. Police and the government do not state a reason for the arrest. (Reuters)
  • Four unauthorized miners are killed in a shooting targeting a vehicle by unidentified gunmen in Barkin Ladi, Plateau State, Nigeria. (Daily Post Nigeria)
  • One child is killed and two others are injured in a stabbing attack in the Blue Mountains of New South Wales, Australia. The children's mother, who was also hospitalised with injuries, is the chief suspect. (The Guardian Australia)
  • Three people are fatally shot and one person is injured in a shooting in a shack in Phumlani informal settlement in Lingelethu West, Philippi, on the Cape Flats, South Africa. (SABC)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Mecklenburg-Vorpommern state election, 2026 Berlin state election
    • State elections are held in Germany for the Landtag of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and the Berlin House of Representatives, with an expected decline for the Chancellor Friedrich Merz's party, the CDU. (BBC News)

Sports

  • 2026 Asian Games
    • Japan at the 2026 Asian Games, Triathlon at the 2026 Asian Games
      • Japanese triathlete Takumi Hojo wins the first gold medal of the 2026 Asian Games. (AFP)
  • 2026 UCI Road World Championships
    • In cycling, Belgian rider Remco Evenepoel becomes the first man to win four consecutive Road World Championship titles in the individual time trial event and equals Fabian Cancellara and Tony Martin's joint record for the most titles. Swiss rider Marlen Reusser wins the women's time trial event. (AFP via The Guardian)

item.title: Current Events - September 13, 2026
item.description:
September 13, 2026 (2026-09-13) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Hezbollah–Israel conflict
      • The Ghana Army says that Battalion 92 of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon will return to Ghana following a year of duty in southern Lebanon. (GhanaWeb)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • A Russian drone attacks a train bound for Warsaw, Poland, at Yahodyn station in western Ukraine, shortly after former UK prime minister Boris Johnson and top EU security officials had passed through the airspace. Former U.S. CIA director David Petraeus was also at the station at the time of the strike but was unharmed. (BBC News)

Disasters and accidents

  • Shipwrecks in 2026
    • Sinking of the Virgo Transport 8
      • Six people die, 97 are rescued and 140 remain missing after the sinking of the Virgo Transport 8 ferry in the Java Sea, Indonesia. (BBC News)
    • Sinking of the MV Matui
      • One person dies, 12 are rescued, and more than 30 remain missing after the sinking of the MV Matui ferry off Espiritu Santo, Vanuatu, during rough seas. (ABC News Australia) (The Guardian)
  • A multiple-vehicle collision on a major highway in Western Cape, South Africa, kills at least 21 people and leaves four others injured, according to the Road Traffic Management Corporation. (AP)

International relations

  • Myanmar's Union Government revokes Kyaw Moe Tun's status as the country's permanent representative to the United Nations, accusing him of illegal activities, as the UN Credentials Committee prepares to consider the country's disputed representation. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • Datu Usman Mampen Elementary School shooting
    • Three people are killed and 15 others are injured when gunfire erupted outside a school in Cotabato City, Bangsamoro, Philippines, used as a polling station for the Bangsamoro Parliament election the following day. Police say that members of rival political factions clashed while competing to be first in line to vote. (AFP via The Star)
  • Mexican drug war
    • Law enforcement agents rescue eight people who they say were forcibly recruited by the Jalisco New Generation Cartel from a clandestine clinic in Tecalitlán, Jalisco, Mexico. Police arrest six suspected guards and seize drugs, weapons, and ammunition. (Al Jazeera)
  • An attack on the Panguna mine in the autonomous region of Bougainville, in Papua New Guinea, injures personnel and destroys equipment amid opposition to plans to reopen the copper mine. (AFP via France 24) (Reuters)
  • Turkish police detain at least 63 people in raids targeting LGBTQ+ organizations and venues across several provinces. The justice ministry says investigations involve 162 suspects, nine associations and 13 businesses over alleged offences including prostitution and obscenity. (Al Jazeera)

Politics and elections

  • 2025–2026 Kosovo political deadlock
    • The Assembly of Kosovo is declared constituted by acting president and speaker Albulena Haxhiu, but without the deputy speaker from the PDK. The Assembly then accepts the fourth cabinet of incumbent prime minister Albin Kurti. The PDK and the AAK both challenge the legitimacy of Kurti's government at the Constitutional Court. (AP) (Reuters)
  • 2026 Swedish general election
    • Swedes vote to elect all 349 seats of the Riksdag. Incumbent prime minister Ulf Kristersson, who seeks to lead the Moderates to a second consecutive government while including the right-wing populist Sweden Democrats in his cabinet, is being challenged by the former prime minister and SAP leader Magdalena Andersson. Preliminary results indicate that the Red-Greens and the Centre Party are projected to have a combined total of 175 seats, while the four Tidö parties are projected to have a total of 174 seats. (AP) (DW)
  • Disinformation in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
    • Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy sanctions his former press secretary, Iuliia Mendel, and nine others for allegedly spreading Russian propaganda and supporting Russia in its war against Ukraine. The 10-year sanctions include asset freezes and trade restrictions. (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2026 Formula One World Championship
    • 2026 Spanish Grand Prix
      • In Formula One racing, Kimi Antonelli wins the inaugural Spanish Grand Prix at the Madring in Madrid, Spain. (ESPN)
  • 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup
    • In basketball, the United States women's team defeats France 97–79 in the final to win the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, Germany, further extending its lead of 12 total wins. (USA Today)
    • American player Breanna Stewart is awarded MVP of the tournament, while Belgian player Emma Meesseman is the top scorer, averaging 21 points per game. (USA Today)
  • 2026 US Open
    • In tennis, Alexander Zverev wins the men's singles title of the 2026 US Open after defeating Ben Shelton in the final, 6–3, 7–6(7–2), 5–7, 6–2. It is his first US Open title and second major title overall. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 Women's Twenty20 Asia Cup
    • In cricket, the India women's team wins its eighth Asia Cup title by defeating Sri Lanka by 72 runs, but refuses to accept the trophy from Asian Cricket Council president and Pakistani interior minister Mohsin Naqvi during the presentation ceremony. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 World Athletics Ultimate Championship
    • In athletics, British middle-distance runner Josh Kerr wins the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship in the 1500 metres event in Budapest, Hungary's National Athletics Centre. (The Independent)
    • Melissa Jefferson-Wooden and Kenny Bednarek win the inaugural women's and men's 200 metres at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship. (The Athletic via The New York Times)

item.title: Current Events - September 19, 2026
item.description:
September 19, 2026 (2026-09-19) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Iran war ceasefire
        • Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaee says that Iran has set seven conditions for resuming ceasefire negotiations with the United States. (Iran International)
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • United States Central Command commander Brad Cooper says that oil, cargo, and liquefied natural gas shipments in the Strait of Hormuz have hit a six-month high. (Bloomberg) (Middle East Eye)
    • Gaza war
      • Israeli airstrikes kill at least three Palestinians in Gaza, including the eldest son of the Gaza Health Ministry director-general. Israel says it targeted militants, while medics report additional deaths in Sheikh Radwan and Shuja'iyya. (Reuters)
  • Operation Southern Spear
    • United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear
      • The U.S. military strikes a vessel in the Caribbean Sea, killing four people whom the Southern Command says were involved in drug trafficking. (Reuters)
  • Islamic State insurgency in the Philippines
    • A series of clashes, involving combined police and military forces and remaining wanted members of the Dawlah Islamiya and the Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Fighters, erupts in Tugunan, Special Geographic Area of the Bangsamoro, Philippines. Seven members from both groups are killed. (The Philippine Star)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
    • Tropical Depression Six forms in the Atlantic Ocean near the Azores amidst an unusually quiet Atlantic hurricane season caused by El Niño. (Fox Weather) (WTSP)
  • 2026 Indonesia wildfires, Indonesia–Malaysia relations
    • Indonesia accepts Malaysian assistance to combat wildfires in Kalimantan, including a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters, and 52 personnel, as the fires cause transboundary haze affecting Southeast Asia. (AFP via France 24)

International relations

  • Eritrea–United States relations
    • The U.S. treasury department lifts the sanctions against Eritrea's ruling party previously imposed by former U.S. president Joe Biden's administration. (AP)
  • 2026 United Nations Secretary-General selection
    • Chilean Michelle Bachelet announces that she is withdrawing from the race to become UN Secretary-General after losing support, and that in the latest informal poll, Costa Rica’s Rebeca Grynspan is reported in the lead. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Domestic violence in South Africa, Sexual violence in South Africa
    • South Africans hold memorial runs and protests after police find the bodies of nine women in Ekurhuleni, Gauteng, over two months. Police investigate possible links between the killings, which renew public concern over violence against women. (Reuters)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Russian legislative election
    • Russian election commission chairperson Ella Pamfilova reports cyberattacks targeting Russia's online voting system during the second day of the parliamentary election and says they are repelled. The Minkomsvyaz separately reports thwarting a sabotage attempt on Far Eastern communication lines. (ABC News Australia)
  • 2026 South Ossetian presidential election
    • Marat Kambolov is declared the winner of the presidential elections in the partially recognized South Ossetia. (Reuters)
  • Donald Trump's conflict with the news media
    • United States president Donald Trump's executive office denies journalists from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico access to the White House and confiscates or disables their press passes, citing their coverage of his administration. (AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer)

Sports

  • 2026 Asian Games
    • The 20th Asian Games are opened by Emperor Naruhito in Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture, Japan. (Reuters)
  • 2026 WNBA season
    • In women's basketball, Atlanta Dream player Angel Reese becomes the first player in Women's National Basketball Association history to reach 500 rebounds in a single season. (Bleacher Report)
  • 2026 World Rugby Pacific Nations Cup
    • In rugby union, hosts Japan win their fourth Pacific Nations Cup title after defeating the defending champions Fiji 20–15 in the final at Chichibunomiya Stadium in Tokyo. (AFP via RFI)

item.title: Current Events - September 12, 2026
item.description:
September 12, 2026 (2026-09-12) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 East–West Crude Oil Pipeline attack, Iran–Iraq relations, Iraq in the 2026 Iran war
        • Iraq closes three border crossings with Iran after Iraqi and Saudi officials said that a drone attack on Saudi Arabia's East–West Crude Oil Pipeline originated from Iraq. (AFP via The Times of Israel)
      • 2026 Iran war ceasefire, Iran–United Arab Emirates relations
        • Iran and the United Arab Emirates sign a joint statement calling for restraint in the war. Additionally, Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi ruler Khaled bin Mohamed Al Nahyan meet at the BRICS summit, the highest profile meeting between the two countries since the war started on February 28. (Al-Monitor) (Hindustan Times)
      • 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan, China in the 2026 Iran war
        • The Wall Street Journal reports that Iran had received Chinese satellite images before launching a July 17 strike on the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan that killed three United States Army soldiers. (AFP via Arab News)
    • Yemeni civil war
      • 2026 Yemen offensives, Strait of Bab al-Mandab crisis
        • Yemeni government forces strike Houthi positions near the port of Mokha, Taiz Governorate, and along the Mokha–Dhubab road, reporting that they destroyed vehicles and weapons and killed Houthi fighters after the group captured the city. (AFP via France 24)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Kryvyi Rih strikes, Odesa strikes, Zaporizhzhia strikes
      • Russian drone strikes across Ukraine kill eight civilians, including two people in Zaporizhzhia, two people at a grocery store in Zhytomyr, one person in Kryvyi Rih, while a "massive attack" targeting the Port of Odesa and surrounding areas wounds at least 28 people. (AP)
    • Eastern front of the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • A Russian drone strikes a civilian vehicle in Kramatorsk, Donetsk Oblast, killing three people. (AP)
  • Mexican drug war
    • Four gunmen and a National Guard agent are killed and another is wounded after an attempted ambush against authorities in Jilotlán de los Dolores, Jalisco, Mexico. (La Jornada in Spanish)

Arts and culture

  • 83rd Venice International Film Festival
    • May el-Toukhy's film Woman Unknown wins the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival in Italy, while Lee Chang-dong's Possible Love and Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor's NAZA win the competition's Grand Jury Prize and Special Jury Prize, respectively. (Japan Today)
  • Rukidi IV, the late king of Uganda's Tooro Kingdom, is buried. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • MV June Aster ship fire
    • The Philippine coast guard confirms that 41 more bodies have been discovered aboard the burned vessel MV June Aster off Coron, Palawan, bringing the death toll from the fire to 76. (AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
    • The Atlantic hurricane season reaches a 103-day record in the satellite era without a hurricane after the season started on June 1, the first since 1941, with the El Niño in the Pacific Ocean being a big factor. (CNN) (The New York Times) (USA Today)

International relations

  • North Korean missile tests
    • North Korea launches a series of SRBM missile tests from Wonsan in response to trilateral Freedom Edge military exercises conducted by Japan, South Korea, and the United States. (Korea JoongAng Daily) (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Cléon derailment
    • French officials investigate if the derailment in Cléon, Seine-Maritime, was caused by sabotage after a fragment of rail was found on the tracks. (AFP via France 24) (BBC News) (RTÉ)
  • Libya's RADA Special Deterrence Forces seize about 100,000 MDMA pills moulded with former leader Muammar Gaddafi's likeness after tracking a shipment smuggled from Europe. Officers find the drugs hidden in a cargo van and refer several suspects to prosecutors. (The Independent)
  • Several residents are arrested after riots erupted yesterday in Kobani, Syria, over the murder of a Kurdish citizen that was blamed on an Arab man, while a prison riot and fire at Kobani prison leaves seven inmates dead. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reports the violence erupted over plans to transfer some prisoners to another prison in Aleppo. (AP) (ABC News)

Politics and elections

  • Protests against Donald Trump
    • Protests against the 2026 Iran war, Gaza war protests, Protests against the second Trump administration
      • Thousands of demonstrators gather in Dublin and Doonbeg, Ireland, against U.S. president Donald Trump's visit to the country and protest against his role in the wars in Iran and Gaza. (Irish Times) (The New York Times)
  • 2026 Saxony-Anhalt state election
    • Protesters gather in Germany across 20 cities against the Alternative for Germany following its victory in the Saxony-Anhalt state election. (Al Jazeera)

Sports

  • 2026 US Open
    • In tennis, Elena Rybakina wins the women's singles title at the US Open, her third major title, after defeating two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka in the final, 6–4, 5–7, 6–2. (AFP via France 24)
    • Christian Harrison and Neal Skupski win the men's doubles title at the US Open without dropping a set in the tournament after defeating Kevin Krawietz and Tim Pütz, 6–4, 7–6(8–6) in the final. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 Summer Youth Olympics
    • The Olympic flame arrives in Dakar, Senegal, ahead of the upcoming Youth Olympic Games, which will be the first Olympic Games held in Africa. (AP)

item.title: Current Events - September 21, 2026
item.description:
September 21, 2026 (2026-09-21) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Disasters and accidents

  • Korean conflict
    • An explosion injures three South Korean military officers during an operation inside the Demilitarized Zone, south of the military demarcation line. The Joint Chiefs of Staff says the cause remains unknown. (AFP via The Peninsula)

Health and environment

  • New Zealand's critically endangered black robin wins Forest & Bird's Bird of the Year competition with more than 26,000 votes out of about 105,000 votes. (AFP)

Law and crime

  • Singapore's Land Transport Authority introduces fines of up to S$500 (US$390) for eating on public buses or placing feet on seats, while severe cleanliness or safety violations can incur penalties of up to S$5,000 (US$3,900). (AFP)

item.title: Current Events - September 14, 2026
item.description:
September 14, 2026 (2026-09-14) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • 2026 Yemen offensives
        • Houthi forces seize control of the Hanish Islands in the Red Sea consolidating the group's control of the strategic sea lane off Yemen's western coast. (AP)
        • Houthi forces advance towards the PLC-controlled cities of Marib and Taiz with heavy clashes underway. (Al Jazeera)
    • Iranian support for the Houthis
      • Gulf states call off planned peace talks with Iran in response to Houthi ballistic missile attacks on Saudi Arabia and Yemeni government forces. (Reuters)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Sudan's Popular Congress Party and Sudan Liberation Movement faction led by Abdul Wahid al-Nur agree to broaden talks aimed at ending the three-year civil war in the country. (Sudan Tribune)

Arts and culture

  • 78th Primetime Emmy Awards
    • American actress Jean Smart wins a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series for her role in Hacks, becoming the first actress to win for every season of a show. (Entertainment Weekly) (Variety)
    • American comedy horror television series Widow's Bay wins 14 Emmys including Outstanding Comedy Series, surpassing the record set by The Studio last year. (The Hollywood Reporter) (Los Angeles Times)

Business and economy

  • Nigeria's Dangote Group launches an initial public offering (IPO) of 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 (US$0.40) each, seeking to raise about ₦2.15 trillion ($1.6 billion) to fund the expansion of the Dangote refinery in Lekki, Lagos State. The sale is set to become Africa's biggest IPO. (AFP via France 24)
  • Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd announce that they will sail more container ships through the Suez Canal. (Reuters)
  • Pope Leo XIV restores salaries for cardinals and senior Vatican City officials to pre-COVID-19-pandemic levels, ending reductions introduced by Pope Francis in 2021. The change took effect September 1, 2026, without retroactive compensation. (The Sun)

Disasters and accidents

  • Indonesia extends the search for eight people, including five journalists, after their speedboat disappeared in the Sunda Strait during a reporting mission on Anak Krakatoa's eruption a week prior. Police await test results to identify a body found on Enggano Island. (AFP via Malay Mail)

Health and environment

  • 2026–2027 El Niño event
    • The World Food Programme reports that Sudan's Darfur region is having its driest rainy season since the 1980s, worsening famine conditions amidst the ongoing civil war. (AFP via Free Malaysia Today)
  • Chile becomes the first country in South America to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies, with the World Health Organization confirming the milestone. (AP)

International relations

  • Separatism in the United Kingdom
    • The First Ministers of Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales meet in Cardiff at a summit to call for their independence from the United Kingdom. (BBC News) (The Guardian)

Law and crime

  • Immigration policy of the second Trump administration
    • United States district judge F. Dennis Saylor IV of Massachusetts postpones new rules limiting stays for international students and journalists, preventing the measures from taking effect while a legal challenge proceeds. (AFP via France 24)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Bangsamoro Parliament election
    • Parliamentary elections are held in the Bangsamoro autonomous region, Philippines, its first since its establishment in 2018. (Al Jazeera)

Science and technology

  • Militarisation of space
    • The United States confirms for the first time that it has deployed a weapon in Earth's orbit. Air Force secretary Troy Meink says the highly classified weapon is necessary to "safeguard U.S. forces" against potential enemy action. (BBC News)

item.title: Current Events - September 18, 2026
item.description:
September 18, 2026 (2026-09-18) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • The IRNA reports that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has hit the Togo-flagged oil tanker Trend as it attempted to pass the Strait of Hormuz. (AFP via FMT) (Al Jazeera)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • 2026 Blue Nile campaign
      • The Sudanese Armed Forces says that they have killed several Rapid Support Forces militants in Sudan's Blue Nile state. The country's defence ministry also confirms the attacks. (Radio Tamazuj)
  • Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
    • 2026 Kohat attack
      • A suicide car bombing outside a mosque located inside a police station in Kohat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, kills at least 31 people, including 16 policemen, and injures at least 100 more. The Hafiz Gul Bahadur Group claims responsibility. (AFP)

Business and economy

  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
      • The Bank of Japan raises its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 1.25%, the highest level since 1995, citing inflation pressures from rising energy costs and a weak yen, and signals further increases. (AFP via France 24)
  • Russia places the local assets of Auchan and Nestlé under temporary administration, transferring their control to Russian firm L.E.V. Management, headed by interior minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev. The government cites the companies' origins in countries it designates as "unfriendly" amid broader seizures of foreign-owned businesses. (CNN)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2024–2026 Cuba blackouts
    • Millions of people are left without electricity in Cuba as a result of a collapse of the country's energy power grid. (AP)

Health and environment

  • Zealand Pharma's drug Zeydovio receives approval by the European Medicines Agency's Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use to treat short bowel syndrome. (Reuters)

International relations

  • Denmark–United States relations
    • Greenland crisis
      • Denmark and the United States reach a deal allowing the U.S. to expand its military presence in Greenland and granting permanent basing, overflight, and access rights, while barring non-NATO countries from establishing bases and restricting sensitive investments on the island. (Reuters)
  • International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war, United States sanctions against Iran
    • U.S. president Donald Trump signs the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which authorises and expands statutory sanctions, tariffs, and prohibitions on Russia and extends existing sanctions on Iran until 2031. (Middle East Eye) (Kyiv Indepedent)
  • Polish prime minister Donald Tusk announces that Poland has joined the Anti-Ballistic Missile Coalition to develop a joint anti-ballistic missile defence system with some other European countries. (Firstpost)

Law and crime

  • 1MDB scandal
    • King Sultan Ibrahim of Malaysia grants former prime minister Najib Razak a conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, following his corruption conviction linked to 1MDB. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Ceuta migrant crisis
    • Spanish police begin moving more than 3,000 migrants from beaches in Ceuta to temporary accommodation at the port. The operation prompts crowding and clashes, with officers firing warning shots and several people sustaining injuries. (News.Az)
  • 2026 South Cotabato school shooting
    • Three students, including the perpetrator, are killed ‌and eight others are injured ​in ​a mass shooting at a ⁠secondary ​school in ​Banga, South Cotabato, Philippines. (AA)
  • Afghanistan–Pakistan relations
    • Pakistan's medical regulator orders Afghan students enrolled in medical and dental programs to leave their colleges and return to Afghanistan. Dozens challenge the directive in court, while a Lahore judge temporarily suspends expulsions in Punjab. (AFP via France 24)
  • Protests erupt in Minna, Niger State, Nigeria, after 37 miners died yesterday in custody of the Security and Civil Defence Corps following raids on suspected illegal mines. Niger state governor Mohammed Umar Bago imposes a curfew. (Reuters)
  • Russia designates filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev a foreign agent, subjecting him to financial restrictions, reporting requirements, and mandatory labels on published material. Zvyagintsev, who lives abroad, has criticized the Russo-Ukrainian war and president Vladimir Putin. (Reuters)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Russian legislative election
    • Russians begin voting to elect 450 seats of the State Duma over a period of three days following Ukrainian attacks upon oil infrastructure. The elections are also held under strict control during the Russo-Ukrainian war, combined with an ongoing crackdown on anti-war opposition and the anti-war party Yabloko being disqualified from running. (AFP via RNZ) (AP)
  • The Senate of Bolivia ratifies an agreement to take a US$1.9 billion loan from the International Monetary Fund amid a deep economic crisis in the country, with trade unions threatening renewed protests in response. (AP)

Science and technology

  • Investigation of UFO reports by the United States government
    • The U.S. Defense Department releases a sixth batch of classified files related to unidentified flying objects, including videos of several orbs flying over Washington, D.C. in 1952 and orbs flying near Tremonton, Utah, also in 1952. (BBC News) (CBC News)

item.title: Current Events - September 11, 2026
item.description:
September 11, 2026 (2026-09-11) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • 2026 Yemen offensives
        • In Yemen, the Houthis seize Perim Island in the Strait of Bab al-Mandab after government forces withdrew, completing their takeover of the surrounding area and giving them control of territory overlooking a major sea lane between the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. (AFP via France 24)
        • The Houthis announce the end and the success of their offensive, expelling government forces from six districts and seizing major locations. (Al Jazeera)
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 East–West Crude Oil Pipeline attack, Saudi Arabia in the 2026 Iran war
        • Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy temporarily closes the East-West Crude Oil Pipeline as a precautionary measure following multiple attacks by drones from Iraq on Thursday. (CNBC)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Ukrainian drone strikes kill two people and injure three others in Tula Oblast, Russia, while a separate strike kills a 37-year-old man in Kursk Oblast, according to regional officials. (Reuters)
    • Kyiv strikes, Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Russian drone strikes hit two petrol stations in Kyiv, Ukraine, killing two people and injuring 12 others. A separate attack on a residential building injures eight people, while another strike kills a woman in Kyiv Oblast. (Reuters)

Arts and culture

  • Princess Astrid, an older sister of the late Norwegian King Harald V and daughter of Olav V, dies at the age of 94. (Nine.com.au) (Sky News)

Business and economy

  • Kyrgyzstan's central bank starts domestically printing banknotes of the Kyrgyz som, the country's currency, for the first time since independence. (24.kg) (Kursiv)

Disasters and accidents

  • MV June Aster ship fire
    • The death toll from the MV June Aster ferry fire off Coron, Palawan, Philippines, rises from five to 35 after firefighters boarded the burned vessel and recovered 30 additional bodies. The coast guard continues searching for dozens of missing passengers and crew. (Reuters)
  • At least 16 people are killed in a fire in a retirement home near Pitrufquén, Cautín, Chile. Ten people are rescued and hospitalized. (DPA via Yahoo News)
  • Thirteen people are killed and eight others are injured when a minibus collided with a car and a logging truck in Kholmogorsky District, Arkhangelsk Oblast, Russia. (Reuters) (Xinhua)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • A case of Ebola is reported in the Sud-Ubangi province, making it the seventh province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo the outbreak has spread to. (The Independent)
  • 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
    • The U.S. Food and Drug Administration and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention declares an end to the cyclosporiasis food poisoning outbreak, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis and linked to iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms, in the United States. (CNBC) (Reuters)
  • Endangerment of orangutans, India–Indonesia relations
    • Indonesia works with Indian authorities to repatriate five baby orangutans found in an Odisha forest after suspected trafficking. Odisha Police and India's Wildlife Crime Control Bureau examine how the apes, which are native to Borneo and Sumatra, reached India. (AFP via France 24)

International relations

  • Nigeria–South Africa relations, Xenophobia in South Africa
    • Nigeria's National Assembly suspends all official visits and virtual engagements with South Africa in protest over repeated anti-migrant attacks there, including violence against Nigerians. (Al Jazeera)
  • Israel–United Kingdom relations
    • In retaliation to British sanctions on goods from Israeli settlements earlier this week, the Israeli government orders a team of British soldiers who train and advise Palestinian Authority security forces in the West Bank to leave the country. (The Telegraph)

Law and crime

  • The Gambia bans protests without official permits after demonstrations over prolonged power outages damaged a police post and utility offices. Police arrest 11 people in connection with the unrest and warn that they will disperse unauthorized gatherings. (Reuters)
  • A Hong Kong court sentences pro-democracy activists Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung to seven years in prison each for inciting subversion under the national security law for leading the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China. (AFP) (Reuters)
  • The Lebanese Army arrests Suleiman Hilal Al Assad, a cousin of former Syrian president Bashar al-Assad, along with two other men, on drug trafficking charges. The men are now under the custody of Lebanon's defence ministry. (AP) (Gulf News)
  • The Seoul Central District Court acquits former South Korean president Yoon Suk Yeol on charges that he appointed his defense minister, Lee Jong-sup, as ambassador to Australia to obstruct an investigation into a South Korean marine's drowning during the 2023 floods. (AP)
  • South Africa extradites six Nigerian nationals allegedly belonging to Black Axe to the United States, where they face wire fraud and money laundering charges linked to online romance scams that allegedly defrauded more than 100 victims. (Reuters)

Politics and elections

  • September 11 intelligence before the attacks
    • The U.S. Central Intelligence Agency releases 71 documents warning of a threat from Al Qaeda prior to the September 11 attacks, including presidential daily briefs during the administrations of former U.S. presidents Bill Clinton and George W. Bush from 1998 to the day after the attacks. (BBC News) (Al Jazeera)
